answers.assumption_check: Load-bearing: (1) parse()'s entry rule (a line opening with a dotted number) survives markdown if the leading '#' or '-' marker is allowed before the number; (2) the conversion keeps every entry's text byte-for-byte apart from the marker and indentation, so a one-time comparison at build against press_office/CairnComponentOutline.txt at a921554bf settles fidelity; (3) the check reads every piece, concatenated in filename order, because finding what a ticket touches needs the whole; reading only touched pieces is a later measured refinement, not this ticket.
answers.builder_check: A Haiku builder needs: (1) file names requirements/NN-<slug>.md, NN the section number zero-padded to two digits, slug from the section title lower-cased with hyphens (00-how-to-read-this.md ... 18-press-office.md); (2) the top line of a section becomes '# N TITLE'; every deeper entry becomes a list item '- <number> <text>' indented two spaces per dot beyond the first (9.4 at 0 spaces, 9.4.2 at 2); continuation lines indent to the item's text; bullet lines inside an item ('- akienasus_cc_0') stay as they are, indented with the item; (3) TOC.md: a heading, then one line per piece '- [NN-slug.md](NN-slug.md): what it holds' in one phrase; (4) outline_check: ENTRY becomes r'^\s*(?:#+\s+|[-*]\s+)?(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\s+(\S.*)$'; outline_file() becomes outline_dir() = roots()['cairn']/'cairn/devices/cairn/requirements'; check() reads sorted(dir.glob('[0-9][0-9]-*.md')) joined with a blank line, outline_path is the folder, outline_sha256 over the joined bytes; (5) fidelity at build: parse(joined pieces) equals parse(git show a921554bf:press_office/CairnComponentOutline.txt) entry for entry, recorded on the verdict, not as a standing tooth (the pieces will be edited); (6) then git rm the .txt, edit 0.9 to name the folder, repoint INDEX.md and skills/sorted/SKILL.md.
